title: Dolly Parton: Science Icon - Nautilus
gist: An obituary-tribute recalling that Dolly the sheep—the first cloned mammal—was named after singer Dolly Parton, who died at 80 and leaves a scientific legacy the piece says extends beyond the cloning joke.

themes.theme: Naming of the first cloned mammal

insights.claim: University of Edinburgh geneticists named Dolly the sheep—the first cloned mammal—after Dolly Parton because the sheep was cloned from a mammary gland cell.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Records the origin of one of science's most famous naming stories.
insights.quote: we couldn’t think of a more impressive pair of glands than Dolly Parton’s.
insights.locator: When geneticists from the University of Edinburgh successfully cloned the first mammal

insights.claim: Dolly Parton died at age 80 following an undisclosed and brief battle with cancer.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Notes the occasion for the tribute.
insights.locator: passed away at the age of 80

insights.claim: Parton responded to her sheep namesake with humor and said she did not want to be cloned herself.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Color that frames her attitude toward the cloning connection.
insights.quote: I was sorry when she died, though I don’t want be cloned myself.
insights.locator: she said in an interview with The Guardian
